cards.text: Samuel is the LORD's prophet (1 Samuel 3:20), and he's still mourning for Saul, the king the LORD has rejected as king over Israel. So the LORD asks him how long he's going to keep mourning. Then He says, "Fill your horn with oil and go."

cards.question: The LORD tells Samuel He is sending him to Jesse of ___.
Samuel's horn is full of oil. Why is the LORD sending him to Jesse's house?

answers.text: He has picked a king from Jesse's sons
He wants Jesse's sons to join the army
He wants Samuel to settle in Jesse's town

cards.text: Saul is still king, and the LORD wants Samuel to go anoint somebody else. That's like training the new manager while the old manager is still in the building with his door WIDE OPEN.

cards.question: Samuel asks the LORD how he can go. What does Samuel say Saul will do if he hears about it?

cards.text: The LORD has a plan: take a heifer along and say, 'I have come to sacrifice to the LORD.' Then invite Jesse to the sacrifice.

cards.question: True or false: the LORD tells Samuel ahead of time exactly which of Jesse's sons to anoint.

cards.text: So Samuel does what the LORD said and goes to Bethlehem, and the town elders come out to meet him TREMBLING. It's like your boss's boss walking in unannounced, and suddenly everybody's standing up straight.

cards.question: What do the trembling elders of Bethlehem ask Samuel?

answers.text: Who else is coming with you

cards.question: Samuel tells the elders he comes in peace. True or false: he leaves Jesse's sons at home and invites only Jesse to the sacrifice.

cards.text: Jesse and his sons arrive, and Samuel spots Eliab, one of Jesse's sons. Samuel takes ONE look.

cards.question: What does Samuel say when he sees Jesse's son Eliab?

answers.text: Surely this is the LORD's anointed
This son is too young to be king
This son looks too much like Saul

cards.text: But the LORD tells Samuel not to consider Eliab's appearance or height, because He has rejected him. Samuel was hiring off the profile picture, and the LORD does NOT hire off the profile picture.

cards.question: The LORD says He does not see as man does. When He picks a king, what is He looking at?

cards.text: Then Jesse calls Abinadab, another son, and presents him to Samuel. It's turned into an audition, and Jesse is the agent.

cards.question: True or false: the LORD chooses Jesse's son Abinadab.

cards.text: Next Jesse presents Shammah, and Samuel says the LORD hasn't chosen him either. Jesse keeps bringing sons forward until seven of them have passed before Samuel.

cards.question: Seven of Jesse's sons have passed before Samuel. How many of them has the LORD chosen?
The LORD still hasn't chosen anyone, so Samuel asks Jesse if these are all the ___ he has.

cards.text: Jesse says there's still the youngest, but he's out tending the sheep. Stuck out back while the big moment happens? Friend, I spent YEARS in the back of a junk drawer, so I FEEL that.

cards.question: Samuel tells Jesse to send for his youngest son. True or false: Samuel says they can sit down to eat while they wait for him.

cards.text: So Jesse sends for his youngest son and brings him in, ruddy, with beautiful eyes and a handsome appearance. Now hold on. Eliab had the looks too, and we saw how THAT went.

cards.question: Jesse's youngest son walks in. What does the LORD tell Samuel?

answers.text: Send him back to the field

cards.text: So Samuel takes the horn of oil and anoints him right in front of his brothers. And the youngest finally gets his name in the story: David.

cards.question: Samuel has anointed David. From that day forward, what rushes upon David?

cards.text: Then Samuel sets out and goes to Ramah. Hang on, friend, because this story is just getting STARTED.

findings.problem: This story card adds no new moment. Cards 1 to 3 already told that Saul was rejected and that a new king is coming from Jesse's sons, and card 4 repeats that and adds a joke. Its 'anoint' detail also comes from 16:3, ahead of Samuel's objection in 16:2. The joke should ride on a card that tells the next piece of the passage, such as Samuel's fear in 16:2, or this card should be cut.

rule.text: Every story card moves the baker forward through the passage. No recap cards. Every story card tells part of the passage. Jokes ride along on those cards.

findings.problem: Samuel's call 'Consecrate yourselves and come with me to the sacrifice,' and his consecrating Jesse and his sons, are never told. Card 10 jumps from 'in peace' straight to who was invited. The consecration is a key step before the anointing scene.

rule.text: When the baker leaves Prep, they understand the whole passage without missing an important detail.

findings.problem: The right answer 'Surely this is the LORD's anointed' sounds like the Bible. The wrong answers, 'This son is too young to be king' and 'This son looks too much like Saul', sound plain and modern, so the right answer stands out.

rule.text: Don't let the right answer stand out. All the answers should sound alike. None should sound more like the Bible, or more modern, than the others.

findings.problem: The answers aren't the same kind of thing. 'sons' and 'servants' are people, but 'flocks' are animals, so 'flocks' is easy to rule out and the question becomes trivial.

rule.text: All the answers are the same kind of thing, about the same length and the same tone. None are silly.
